provider: Fastly free account + Fast Forward OSS programme

free_tier.stated: Free account: 100 GB bandwidth/month free across all regions, 1M CDN requests/month, 5 domains, 100K purge requests. Above 100 GB: $0.12/GB EU/NA, $0.19/GB Asia/Australia, $0.28/GB Africa/India/South Korea. Fast Forward (OSS/nonprofit programme) has **no published byte quota** — 'we extend free services to eligible open source projects and nonprofits that support them', scope agreed after human review of a Google Form application.

egress.terms: 100 GB/mo free, then metered per region. Fast Forward absorbs bandwidth for accepted projects but is the only path to meaningful volume.

tooling: VCL / Compute@Edge; standard HTTP origin pull. Free accounts are self-serve at fastly.com/signup.
chaining: 100 GB/month = 3.3 GB/day: an order of magnitude too small to matter for serving, so the free tier is a *test bench*, not a lane. Fast Forward is the only Fastly path to real capacity and it is gated on being a recognised open-source project with an OSI licence and public documentation — i.e. it is a legitimate way to get a big free CDN for an OSS artefact but not for a private 20 TiB archive.

limits.value: review of a Google Form application

limits_note: per-object-cap: none. The binding limit is the 100 GB/month counter (and 1M requests). Fast Forward: discretionary human acceptance, no published SLA, and the previous '$50/month of free traffic' credit model was retired for new accounts created after 2025-10-28.
reliability_note: Bandwidth is metered per *region* with no pooling, so a geographically mixed audience burns the 100 GB fastest. Fast Forward is real (PyPI, Rust Foundation, PSF, Kubernetes, Mastodon, 100+ projects) and worth applying to if any of the client's datasets ship as a public OSS artefact.
